I will keep doing what is most steady and familiar for me here in Quzhou: I will plant a winter wheat and summer maize rotation. That is the crop path I trust most on this land. I am 76, so I do not want to spread myself across too many crops or take on crops that need fine management every day. Wheat and maize fit our local water, soil, and market conditions, and I know how to handle them with simple, proven steps.

At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so my main job now is to manage it well through spring. I will topdress nitrogen, water at the key stages if water is available, and watch for aphids, rust, and weeds. I will not overdo inputs, because I want stable yield more than risk. After wheat harvest in early summer, I will move quickly into summer maize. I will use hybrid maize seed because it gives me a more reliable harvest. To save labor and catch soil moisture, I will do minimal tillage for maize after wheat, put on fertilizer in a simple way, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and spray only when pest pressure is real. I will keep the whole year simple, practical, and manageable for my age.
